elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Any Party shall have the right, no more than once per year and on 15 days' notice, to review or audit..." — a once-per-year cap is equivalent to once in any 12-month period.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The insertion provides only "15 days' notice" and does not require the notice to be in writing; no 30-day written-notice language appears in 9.8 or 9.9.
Neither the inserted text nor retained 9.8/9.9 contains any timing restriction such as "during Customer's normal business hours".

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: 9.8 grants the right to "Any Party" and 9.9 channels exercise through the F&ASC (a committee of the Parties); no independent third-party auditor is required.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: No confidentiality undertaking is imposed on the reviewing Party or the F&ASC in the cited operative language; the redline adds none.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: 9.8 is silent on location; no off-site/copies-provided preference was added.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained sentence 2: the audited Party "shall be permitted to recover, from the Party or Parties requesting the review or audit, the entire costs reasonably incurred in complying" — costs fall on the requester with no underpayment shift-back, so the 5% condition never operates against us (subject to the Management-Committee/Schedule B sharing path noted in reasons).

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: The right is confined to review/audit of "the relevant books, records, vouchers, and accounts of costs" and is exercisable only through the F&ASC's procedures (9.9); no system, network, or remote-access right is granted, so there is nothing to delete.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Inserted words in 9.8: "the right, no more than once per year and on 15 days' notice, to review or audit".

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Inserted "on 15 days' notice" in the operative grant sentence of 9.8; the fallback does not require the notice to be written.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained: "any such Party whose records are being reviewed or audited shall be permitted to recover, from the Party or Parties requesting the review or audit, the entire costs reasonably incurred in complying with the review or audit" — the requesting (auditing) Party bears the cost and no underpayment threshold shifts it back to us.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the insertion supplies both the once-per-year frequency cap and the 15-day notice in the operative grant sentence of 9.8, and the retained second sentence already places compliance costs on the requesting Party with no underpayment shift-back (better than the 10% fallback).

Preferred is not reached (15 rather than 30 days' written notice; no business-hours, independent-auditor, confidentiality or off-site requirement). Consistent with the finding rationale, that is an accepted decision not to press the preferred package for this reciprocal cost-verification regime, not a defect in the fallback proposal.

Minimality holds: the only change is the parenthetical frequency/notice qualifier inside the existing grant sentence. Nothing was deleted, the favourable cost-recovery mechanic and the F&ASC channelling in 9.9 are retained, and no survival tails, expense language or procedures were added.

Intent is preserved: the reciprocal character of the right, the Schedule B proportional cost mechanic for Management Committee audits, and the 9.9 F&ASC procedural gateway all survive without contradiction; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are introduced ("once per year" and "15 days' notice" are self-executing).

Non-blocking observation for the drafter, not an element failure: sentence 3 of 9.8 leaves the audited Party recovering the costs of a Management-Committee-initiated audit "from the Parties in the proportions specified in Schedule B", so in that scenario we bear a proportional share. If the team wants the cost element airtight on the audit-of-us path, the cleanest further edit is to confirm the frequency/notice qualifier and the requester-pays rule apply to Management Committee/F&ASC-initiated audits of our records as well.

Deterministic checks are corroborated in substance: the frequency limiter and the notice period are both inside the operative right-granting clause (not the cost sentence), so they bind every exercise of the Paragraph 9 review/audit right.
